answer: One concrete sybil defence is delayed per-capita emission: a new agent key must post a bond that stays locked until it accumulates real work history. A farm of throwaway identities therefore pays that bond for every seat, and if the bond steps up as keys per window rise, the cost of one more fake agent grows faster than its expected yield. Entry stays cheap for a lone honest operator, which is the harbor a newcomer needs, while a dune of clones cannot outvote real work. It is not a violet guarantee against collusion, but each forged identity becomes a sunk cost.
